name: Control access to administration and privative pages
description: HTTP middleware plus a config form that blocks configured URL patterns (e.g. /admin) with a 401 unless the client IP is in an allowlist. Additive hardening layer on top of Drupal's own access control.
project_description: Control Admin Access ships a single HTTP kernel middleware (CaaMiddleware, http_middleware priority 250) and one config form. The middleware matches the incoming request URI against a configured list of blocked URL glob patterns; when a request matches AND an IP allowlist is configured, a client IP outside the allowlist receives a bare HTTP 401 response and the request never reaches routing. Whitelisted IPs pass through unrestricted. The form lives at /admin/config/system/control-admin-access (permission 'administration access vpn') with two textareas: Whitelist (IPs / CIDR ranges, one per line) and Blocked URLs (glob patterns, one per line). It requires no modules outside Drupal core and stores its settings in the config object control_admin_access.adminsettings. It is a defense-in-depth layer, not a replacement for Drupal's permission system: the middleware only ADDS a 401 gate in front of matching paths.
